🛡️ KeyShield · Manual Verify Hub

Drop the unpacked extension into Chrome, open each fixture, and walk the checklist below. These pages are inert — the keys are synthetic and do nothing.

Fixtures

happyOpenAI dashboard
One key in a password field, page styled like platform.openai.com.
 happyHelius RPC
UUID-shaped key inline as ?api-key=….
 happyStripe keys
Two fields: publishable + secret. Auto-detect should label both.
 paste.env paste
Textarea pre-filled with 4 secrets. Tests multi-key extraction.
 trapFalse-positive trap
UUIDs, JWTs, git SHAs, “openai” in prose. Should NOT alert.

Checklist

Open each page in order. For each item, verify the listed behaviour.

Detection

  1. OpenAI page — toast appears within ~3 s with provider OpenAI.
  2. Helius page — toast labels the UUID match as Helius.
  3. Stripe page — one toast for the secret sk_live_…; the publishable pk_live_… may auto-suppress (lower priority).
  4. .env paste — opening the popup right after the page loads shows ≥ 3 distinct providers staged.
  5. Trap page — no toast appears for at least 5 s.

One-click save

  1. Click Save on the OpenAI toast — toast disappears, popup vault list shows OpenAI entry.
  2. Reopen the popup after closing — the saved entry persists (cache hit).
  3. Click × to dismiss the Helius toast — toast removed, popup does NOT gain a Helius entry.
  4. Auto-dismiss timing — if you ignore a toast, it disappears on its own around 10 s.

Cross-device sanity (optional, requires VITE_KEYSHIELD_SYNC_URL)

  1. Save a key on Chrome A.
  2. On Chrome B with the same passkey, reopen the popup — the same entry is there after a pull.

How to load the extension

Option A — download the prebuilt extension (only on the GitHub Pages deploy; this link 404s in local file:// preview):

⬇ keyshield-extension.zip

Unzip it, then:

  1. Open chrome://extensions
  2. Toggle Developer mode (top-right)
  3. Click Load unpacked → pick the unzipped folder

Option B — build from source:

cd extension-sync
npm install
npm run build:ext          # produces dist/ with manifest.json + everything
# Chrome: chrome://extensions  →  Developer mode  →  Load unpacked  →  pick dist/

All keys on these pages are synthetic patterns — they will not authenticate against any real provider. Treat them like passwords anyway in case you ever copy this folder somewhere unexpected.
